keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 macro nature photo. One thick young green bamboo culm stands upright in the center and fills about 70 percent of the frame width, with a soft out-of-focus green bamboo grove behind it. At about one sixth of the frame height from the top there is a bamboo node, a slightly raised ring around the culm. Directly below this node, a tall oval window is cut into the front wall of the culm, from just below the node down to about 55 percent of the frame height. Through the window we see inside the hollow internode: the flat underside of the node forms the ceiling at the top, and the inside of the culm wall is lined with soft, moist, creamy white pulp. The cut edge of the window shows the thickness of the green bamboo wall. The hollow is empty. Below the window, at about 60 percent of the frame height, there is one small round hole in the front of the culm, about one ninth of the culm width wide. At about two thirds of the frame height is the next node, and from this node down to the bottom of the frame the culm is wrapped in a papery light brown bamboo culm sheath with fine dark hairs. On this sheath, just below the node and under the hole, lies one small flat patch of tiny oval light brown eggs that overlap each other like fish scales. The egg patch is about one eighth of the culm width wide. Soft daylight, everything clearly lit, including the inside of the hollow, sharp focus. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the bamboo culm, the nodes, the oval window, the empty hollow, the small round hole, the sheath, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The eggs have hatched: the egg patch is now pale, empty, see-through egg shells in the same spot. About twelve tiny newly hatched caterpillars crawl on the sheath right next to the empty shells, heading up toward the small round hole. Each caterpillar is dark brown with a black stripe along its back and long thin bright white hairs, and is about one fifteenth of the culm width long. No text, no watermark.

The tiny caterpillars are gone from the sheath. Inside the hollow, seen through the window, four small young caterpillars now lie side by side on the creamy white pulp near the bottom of the window. They are milky white with a small brown head, and each is about one eighth of the culm width long. Only four caterpillars. No text, no watermark.

The pulp lower in the hollow is eaten away. Only four caterpillars. No text, no watermark.
